summary: Fallback-concurrency inversion causing reserved-pool burst starvation and degraded p99
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a reserved pool reported a midday spike where short-lived streaming requests abruptly routed to a lower-capacity fallback model variant, causing a cascade: fallback instances consumed disproportionate GPU attach slots, triggering allocator backpressure and a persistent p99 uplift across the pool. Impact is sustained for ~20-40 minutes during these windows.

Impact:
- NimbleDocs (dedicated) observed p99 latency increase from 180ms -> 860ms for short streaming calls.
- Throughput (tokens/sec) dropped by ~35% across the pool during incidents.
- Automatic fallback to quantized/low-memory model variants appears to be correlated with the start of the window.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (prod, us-east) serving redwood/gptx-13b-v2 (pinned) with automatic fallback policies enabled.
- Autoscaler: predictive + reactive with default attach concurrency of 4.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Send 3k short streaming requests (avg 60 tokens) over a 5 minute window.
2) Observe routing: when main nodes temporarily report KV-cache warmup >10s, the router pushes to fallback variant.
3) Fallback attaches are short-lived but allocate NVLink/slot resources and prevent main pool attach convergence, leading to queueing and higher p99.

Logs & key traces:
- Router trace: fallback decision spikes at 11:07:12 - 11:07:55 UTC (see router.trace ids in comments).
- Autoscaler events: series of rapid attach/fail/attach at 11:07:xx producing allocator contention.
- Serving runtime logs: repeated "attach_slot_timeout" and "kv-cache-miss" messages correlated with fallback attach bursts.

Observed hypothesis:
We believe a concurrency inversion occurs when the fallback variant has faster cold attach success for short streams but higher slot-churn per attach. Because the router prefers lower-latency attach for short requests, many requests temporarily route to fallback, causing many rapid attach/detach operations that fragment slot availability and delay main model prefetch/warmup. The autoscaler interprets attach failures as capacity pressure and tightens attach throttles, exacerbating the throughput drop.

Customer impact notes:
- Customer reports business KPIs affected (search indexing throughput).
- Customer requested immediate mitigation and a durable fix to avoid repeated mid-day degradations.

investigation_notes: 11:15 UTC: Correlated router decisions with kv-cache miss rate; main model firing prefetches but slow warmup correlated with io-wait on nvme (see infra dashboard).

11:22 UTC: Autoscaler attached/detached rapidly; attach success rate for fallback variant ~92% but average attach duration shorter (~120ms) vs main (~280ms), resulting in more frequent churn for equal request volume.

11:45 UTC: NVLink usage and slot allocation patterns show many short-duration attachments from the fallback pool fragmenting allocation windows. Evidence captured in allocator.logs (ids in related_github_prs).
resolution:
Workaround applied: temporarily increased fallback attach backoff, added a routing safety gate to prefer warmed main model when recent prefetch attempts are in-flight, and increased min-attach-duration threshold for fallback variants in dedicated pools.

Immediate result: p99 reduced to ~220ms in the monitored window and throughput recovered to within 95% of baseline.

Long-term actions:
- Engineering will add a routing hysteresis to avoid mass-fallback during short cache warmup periods (tracker PR & follow-up).
- Autoscaler will be updated to better distinguish high churn short attaches vs true capacity shortage.
- Runbook update: add a dedicated-pool fallback throttle knob for customers with high short-stream traffic.

Follow-ups: see linked GH PRs and Confluence pages for implementation plan and rollout schedule.
